Subject: Sierra Dedicated: implementation roadmap & regional burst policy choices

Hi Sara —

Thanks again for the time today. Per our sync, I wanted to capture an initial implementation roadmap and the key decisions we'll need from Sierra to finalize provisioning the Dedicated GPU pool and autoscale/burst policies. High level: provisioning, autoscale/burst thresholds, fallback regions, and compliance items for activation.

Quick asks for this week:
- Confirm preferred primary region (us-west-2 vs us-east-1) and any hard constraints for data residency.
- Share expected 95th percentile qps/token footprint during business hours (estimate fine).
- Agree on default autoscale policy: we propose baseline pool sized for steady load + automatic burst to 2x for spikes, and a conservative canary (10% traffic) for the first 48 hours.

I've attached a first-draft MOP and a template for pool sizing — Karthik and Monica are copied to sketch sizing and the activation runbook. Sean will own ops handoff.

Proposed next step: 60-minute technical kickoff on Wed 3/24 or Thu 3/25 to lock policies and schedule the activation sprint. What works for you?

Thanks —
Aisha Rahman
Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: sierra-mop-v1.pdf (pdf, draft), proposed-pool-sizing.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Sara Kline <sara.kline@sierrahealth.com>

Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sierra Dedicated: implementation roadmap & regional burst policy choices

Thanks Aisha — appreciate the note. A few clarifications from our side before the kickoff:

1) Region: our data residency preference is us-east-1 for the primary pool but we can accept us-west-2 as a fallback for non-PHI workloads.
2) Traffic profile: our initial beta expects 5–8 qps at peak with average request sizes ~600 tokens. We expect daily peak windows 9am–6pm ET.
3) Autoscale: your 2x burst sounds reasonable but can you confirm the cooldown behavior and max-burst billing implications? We have a hard cap budget for burst spend.

Also, security asks: Alan will follow up with a filled security questionnaire and there may be an org SSO/SCIM requirement. I'll attach our procurement checklist.

Wed 3/24 afternoon (ET) works for a kickoff.

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Sara Kline <sara.kline@sierrahealth.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sierra Dedicated: implementation roadmap & regional burst policy choices

Thanks Sara — good specifics. A few technical notes from the infra side (sketching options so we can finalize in the kickoff):

- Primary region: we can provision the primary Dedicated pool in us-east-1 with a warm standby in us-west-2. Standby will not serve PHI by default; we'll set routing policy to prefer primary and fail over to standby only when a) primary capacity saturated OR b) a zone-level incident is detected.
- Baseline pool sizing: based on 8 qps, 600-token average, and model L latency ~50ms, a conservative starting pool is 4x A100 equivalents (we'll produce exact GPU counts in the sizing workbook).
- Autoscale policy proposal: scale up in 10% increments based on sustained CPU/GPU utilization > 70% for 60s, allow burst up to 2x baseline for short spikes (<5min); cooldown 300s. We can add a hard budget cap that triggers a controlled shedding policy or fallback to a cheaper model variant.
- Canary & rollout: 10% traffic canary for first 48h, then 25% for next 48h before full cutover. Automatic rollback if 95th latency or error rates exceed thresholds.

I'll attach a starter pool-sizing sheet and a short ops-runbook for activation. Monica, Sean — can you confirm who will own the post-cutover runbook updates and SLA monitoring?

- Karthik
Principal Inference Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: proposed-pool-sizing.xlsx (xlsx)
